The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

"""Tests for batch verification and cross-site aggregation of chain fork
decisions.

Covers :func:`verify_chain_fork_decisions`,
:func:`aggregate_chain_fork_decisions` and
:func:`verify_chain_fork_decision_aggregate`: the decision batch
container and shared materials validated in full before any decision is
parsed, the per-decision verified/invalid/unauthenticated taxonomy with
input-order reports and no cross-decision interference, the
verify-then-authenticate-then-authorize per-decision aggregation
pipeline with its fixed invalid/unauthenticated/unauthorized reasons,
same-site duplicate/contradiction handling over the complete
declaration (the common fork edge set, the per-item conclusions sorted
by site then id, the term-by-term proof digest vector and the overall
status), cross-site declaration agreement with no majority override,
threshold acceptance with the common declaration kept on insufficient
tallies, the canonical signed aggregate packet and its three policy
digest bindings, the offline re-tally verification recomputing every
binding plus each counted declaration, the aggregate credential rules,
the InvalidChainDecisionAggregateError hierarchy, equal-but-independent
results, input immutability and the purely offline guarantee.
"""

import copy
import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys
import unittest
from unittest import mock

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

from offline_coordination.replication import (
    AuthenticationError,
    InvalidChainDecisionAggregateError,
    InvalidChainDecisionError,
    adjudicate_chain_forks,
    aggregate_chain_fork_decisions,
    verify_chain_fork_decision,
    verify_chain_fork_decisions,
    verify_chain_fork_decision_aggregate,
)

from test_adjudicate_prune_aggregate_forks import proof_item, rewrap
from test_aggregate_prune_fork_decisions import (
    decision_item,
    decision_site_policy,
)
from test_chain_fork_proofs import ChainForkFixtures
from test_fork_convergence import SECRET_COORD, compact, entry, parse
from test_prune_attestations import JUDGE, SITE_A, SITE_B, SITE_C

JUDGE_B = SITE_C
BATCH_REPORT_KEYS = ["items", "version"]
ITEM_REPORT_KEYS = ["error", "id", "result", "status"]
AGGREGATE_KEYS = ["payload", "signature"]
AGGREGATE_PAYLOAD_KEYS = [
    "decisionSitePolicyDigest", "declaration", "inputs", "issuer",
    "items", "keyVersion", "prunePolicyDigest", "sitePolicyDigest",
    "status", "version",
]
AGGREGATE_ROW_KEYS = [
    "conclusion", "declaration", "digest", "id", "issuer", "keyVersion",
    "reason",
]
DECLARATION_KEYS = ["common", "conclusions", "proofs", "status"]
DECLARATION_ENTRY_KEYS = [
    "conclusion", "digest", "edges", "id", "issuer", "reason",
]
AGGREGATE_RESULT_KEYS = [
    "aggregateDigest", "inputs", "issuer", "items", "keyVersion",
    "prunePolicyDigest", "sitePolicyDigest", "decisionSitePolicyDigest",
    "declaration", "status", "version",
]
SINGLE_RESULT_KEYS = [
    "common", "proofDigest", "issuer", "items", "keyVersion",
    "prunePolicyDigest", "proofs", "sitePolicyDigest", "status", "version",
]


class ChainForkDecisionAggregateFixtures(ChainForkFixtures):
    """Signed chain fork decisions from two decision sites and helpers."""

    def setUp(self):  # noqa: D102
        super().setUp()
        self.dsp = decision_site_policy(sites=(JUDGE, JUDGE_B))
        self.proofs = [
            proof_item("x", self.cproof(issuer=SITE_A)),
            proof_item("y", self.cproof(issuer=SITE_B)),
        ]
        self.decision_a = self.make_decision(self.proofs, issuer=JUDGE)
        self.decision_b = self.make_decision(self.proofs, issuer=JUDGE_B)

    def other_proofs(self):
        return [
            proof_item("x", self.cproof(self.cf_items_two, issuer=SITE_A)),
            proof_item("y", self.cproof(issuer=SITE_B)),
        ]

    def decision_items(self):
        return [
            decision_item("one", self.decision_a),
            decision_item("two", self.decision_b),
        ]

    def batch_report(self, items, sp=None, ring=None, moment=None):
        return verify_chain_fork_decisions(
            items, self.policy, self.sp if sp is None else sp,
            self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m if moment is None else moment,
        )

    def make_aggregate(self, items, sp=None, dsp=None, ring=None,
                       moment=None, issuer=JUDGE, version=1):
        return aggregate_chain_fork_decisions(
            items, self.policy, self.sp if sp is None else sp,
            self.dsp if dsp is None else dsp,
            self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m if moment is None else moment, issuer, version,
        )

    def verify_aggregate(self, raw, sp=None, dsp=None, ring=None,
                         moment=None):
        return verify_chain_fork_decision_aggregate(
            raw, self.policy, self.sp if sp is None else sp,
            self.dsp if dsp is None else dsp,
            self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m if moment is None else moment,
        )

    def aggregate_payload(self, items, **kwargs):
        return parse(self.make_aggregate(items, **kwargs))["payload"]


class BatchVerificationTest(ChainForkDecisionAggregateFixtures):
    def test_verified_reports_in_input_order(self):
        report = self.batch_report([
            decision_item("a", self.decision_a),
            decision_item("b", b"{}"),
            decision_item("c", self.decision_b),
        ])
        self.assertEqual(list(report.keys()), BATCH_REPORT_KEYS)
        self.assertEqual(report["version"], 1)
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in report["items"]],
                         ["a", "b", "c"])
        self.assertEqual([row["status"] for row in report["items"]],
                         ["verified", "invalid", "verified"])
        for row in report["items"]:
            self.assertEqual(list(row.keys()), ITEM_REPORT_KEYS)
        good = report["items"][0]
        self.assertIsNone(good["error"])
        self.assertEqual(good["result"]["proofDigest"],
                         hashlib.sha256(self.decision_a).hexdigest())
        self.assertEqual(list(good["result"].keys()), SINGLE_RESULT_KEYS)
        self.assertEqual(good["result"]["issuer"], JUDGE)
        bad = report["items"][1]
        self.assertIsNone(bad["result"])
        self.assertIsInstance(bad["error"], str)
        self.assertNotEqual(bad["error"], "")

    def test_unauthenticated_is_isolated(self):
        ring = {
            site: [entry(1, "77" * 32)]
            for site in (SITE_A, SITE_B, SITE_C, JUDGE)
        }
        report = self.batch_report([
            decision_item("a", self.decision_a),
            decision_item("b", self.decision_b),
        ], ring=ring)
        self.assertEqual([row["status"] for row in report["items"]],
                         ["unauthenticated", "unauthenticated"])
        self.assertTrue(all(row["error"] for row in report["items"]))
        self.assertTrue(all(row["result"] is None
                            for row in report["items"]))

    def test_structure_validated_upfront(self):
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.batch_report("x")
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.batch_report(["x"])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.batch_report([])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.batch_report([
                decision_item("a", self.decision_a),
                decision_item("a", self.decision_b),
            ])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.batch_report([
                {"id": "a", "decision": self.decision_a, "x": 1},
            ])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.batch_report([decision_item("", self.decision_a)])
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.batch_report([decision_item(1, self.decision_a)])
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.batch_report([decision_item("a", "x")])

    def test_shared_materials_validated_upfront(self):
        items = [decision_item("a", self.decision_a)]
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify_chain_fork_decisions(
                items, {"batch": "x"}, self.sp, self.ring, self.m)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify_chain_fork_decisions(
                items, self.policy, {"sites": {}}, self.ring, self.m)
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            verify_chain_fork_decisions(
                items, self.policy, self.sp, "ring", self.m)
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            verify_chain_fork_decisions(
                items, self.policy, self.sp, self.ring, True)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify_chain_fork_decisions(
                items, self.policy, self.sp, self.ring, -1)

    def test_batch_fault_surfaces_even_when_a_decision_is_bad(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.batch_report([
                decision_item("a", b"{}"), decision_item("a", b"{"),
            ])

    def test_one_failure_matches_the_single_decision_result(self):
        report = self.batch_report([
            decision_item("ok", self.decision_a),
            decision_item("bad", b"{}"),
        ])
        single = verify_chain_fork_decision(
            self.decision_a, self.policy, self.sp, self.ring, self.m)
        self.assertEqual(report["items"][0]["result"], single)

    def test_results_are_fresh_and_independent(self):
        items = [decision_item("a", self.decision_a)]
        first = self.batch_report(items)
        second = self.batch_report(items)
        self.assertEqual(first, second)
        self.assertIsNot(first, second)
        self.assertIsNot(first["items"][0]["result"],
                         second["items"][0]["result"])
        first["items"][0]["result"]["issuer"] = "tampered"
        self.assertEqual(
            self.batch_report(items)["items"][0]["result"]["issuer"], JUDGE)

    def test_inputs_are_not_modified(self):
        items = [decision_item("a", self.decision_a)]
        snapshot = copy.deepcopy((items, self.policy, self.sp, self.ring))
        self.batch_report(items)
        self.assertEqual((items, self.policy, self.sp, self.ring), snapshot)


class AggregationValidationTest(ChainForkDecisionAggregateFixtures):
    def test_items_container_and_value_faults(self):
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_aggregate("x")
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_aggregate(["x"])
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_aggregate([decision_item(1, self.decision_a)])
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_aggregate([decision_item("a", 1)])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_aggregate([])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_aggregate([decision_item("", self.decision_a)])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_aggregate([
                decision_item("a", self.decision_a),
                decision_item("a", self.decision_b),
            ])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_aggregate([
                {"id": "a", "decision": self.decision_a, "x": 1},
            ])

    def test_policy_faults(self):
        items = self.decision_items()
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            aggregate_chain_fork_decisions(
                items, {"batch": "x"}, self.sp, self.dsp, self.ring,
                self.m, JUDGE, 1)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_aggregate(items, sp={"sites": {SITE_A: {1}}})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_aggregate(items, dsp={"sites": {JUDGE: {1}}})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_aggregate(items, dsp={"sites": {}, "threshold": 1})
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_aggregate(
                items, dsp={"sites": {JUDGE: [1]}, "threshold": 1})
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_aggregate(
                items, dsp={"sites": {JUDGE: {True}}, "threshold": 1})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_aggregate(
                items, dsp={"sites": {JUDGE: {0}}, "threshold": 1})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_aggregate(
                items, dsp={"sites": {JUDGE: set()}, "threshold": 1})
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_aggregate(
                items, dsp={"sites": {JUDGE: {1}}, "threshold": True})

"""Tests for batch verification and cross-site aggregation of chain fork
aggregate decisions.

Covers :func:`verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions`,
:func:`aggregate_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions` and
:func:`verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decision_aggregate`: the decision
batch container and shared materials validated in full before any
decision is parsed, the per-decision verified/invalid/unauthenticated
taxonomy with input-order reports and no cross-decision interference,
the verify-then-authenticate-then-authorize per-decision aggregation
pipeline with its fixed invalid/unauthenticated/unauthorized reasons,
same-site duplicate/contradiction handling over the complete
declaration (the common fork edge set, the per-item conclusions sorted
by site then id, the original-order proof digest vector and the
overall status), cross-site declaration agreement with no majority
override, threshold acceptance with the common declaration kept on
insufficient tallies, the canonical signed aggregate packet and its
three policy digest bindings, the offline re-tally verification
recomputing every binding plus each counted declaration, the aggregate
credential rules, the distinct
InvalidChainForkDecisionAggregateError hierarchy, equal-but-independent
results, input immutability and the purely offline guarantee.
"""

import copy
import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys
import unittest
from unittest import mock

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

from offline_coordination.replication import (
    AuthenticationError,
    InvalidChainDecisionAggregateError,
    InvalidChainDecisionError,
    InvalidChainForkDecisionAggregateError,
    adjudicate_chain_fork_aggregate_proofs,
    aggregate_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions,
    verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decision,
    verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions,
    verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decision_aggregate,
)

from test_adjudicate_prune_aggregate_forks import proof_item, rewrap
from test_aggregate_prune_fork_decisions import (
    decision_item,
    decision_site_policy,
)
from test_chain_fork_aggregate_proofs import ChainForkAggregateFixtures
from test_fork_convergence import SECRET_COORD, compact, entry, parse
from test_prune_attestations import JUDGE, SITE_A, SITE_B, SITE_C

JUDGE_B = SITE_C
BATCH_REPORT_KEYS = ["items", "version"]
ITEM_REPORT_KEYS = ["error", "id", "result", "status"]
AGGREGATE_KEYS = ["payload", "signature"]
AGGREGATE_PAYLOAD_KEYS = [
    "authorizationPolicyDigest", "decisionSitePolicyDigest",
    "declaration", "inputs", "issuer", "items", "keyVersion",
    "prunePolicyDigest", "status", "version",
]
AGGREGATE_ROW_KEYS = [
    "conclusion", "declaration", "digest", "id", "issuer", "keyVersion",
    "reason",
]
DECLARATION_KEYS = ["common", "conclusions", "proofs", "status"]
DECLARATION_ENTRY_KEYS = [
    "conclusion", "digest", "edges", "id", "issuer", "reason",
]
AGGREGATE_RESULT_KEYS = [
    "aggregateDigest", "inputs", "issuer", "items", "keyVersion",
    "prunePolicyDigest", "authorizationPolicyDigest",
    "decisionSitePolicyDigest", "declaration", "status", "version",
]
SINGLE_RESULT_KEYS = [
    "common", "proofDigest", "issuer", "items", "keyVersion",
    "prunePolicyDigest", "proofs", "authorizationPolicyDigest",
    "status", "version",
]


class ChainForkAggregateDecisionAggregateFixtures(ChainForkAggregateFixtures):
    """Signed chain fork aggregate decisions from two decision sites."""

    def setUp(self):  # noqa: D102
        super().setUp()
        self.dsp = decision_site_policy(sites=(JUDGE, JUDGE_B))
        self.proofs = [
            proof_item("x", self.aproof(issuer=SITE_A)),
            proof_item("y", self.aproof(issuer=SITE_B)),
        ]
        self.decision_a = self.make_cfa_decision(self.proofs, issuer=JUDGE)
        self.decision_b = self.make_cfa_decision(self.proofs, issuer=JUDGE_B)

    def make_cfa_decision(self, proofs, auth=None, ring=None, moment=None,
                          issuer=JUDGE, version=1):
        return adjudicate_chain_fork_aggregate_proofs(
            proofs, self.policy, self.sp,
            self.cauth() if auth is None else auth,
            self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m if moment is None else moment, issuer, version,
        )

    def other_proofs(self):
        return [
            proof_item("x", self.aproof(self.cf_items_two, issuer=SITE_A)),
            proof_item("y", self.aproof(issuer=SITE_B)),
        ]

    def cfa_decision_items(self):
        return [
            decision_item("one", self.decision_a),
            decision_item("two", self.decision_b),
        ]

    def batch_report(self, items, auth=None, ring=None, moment=None):
        return verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions(
            items, self.policy, self.cauth() if auth is None else auth,
            self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m if moment is None else moment,
        )

    def make_cfa_aggregate(self, items, auth=None, dsp=None, ring=None,
                       moment=None, issuer=JUDGE, version=1):
        return aggregate_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions(
            items, self.policy, self.cauth() if auth is None else auth,
            self.dsp if dsp is None else dsp,
            self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m if moment is None else moment, issuer, version,
        )

    def verify_aggregate(self, raw, auth=None, dsp=None, ring=None,
                         moment=None):
        return verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decision_aggregate(
            raw, self.policy, self.cauth() if auth is None else auth,
            self.dsp if dsp is None else dsp,
            self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m if moment is None else moment,
        )

    def aggregate_payload(self, items, **kwargs):
        return parse(self.make_cfa_aggregate(items, **kwargs))["payload"]


class BatchVerificationTest(
    ChainForkAggregateDecisionAggregateFixtures
):
    def test_verified_reports_in_input_order(self):
        report = self.batch_report([
            decision_item("a", self.decision_a),
            decision_item("b", b"{}"),
            decision_item("c", self.decision_b),
        ])
        self.assertEqual(list(report.keys()), BATCH_REPORT_KEYS)
        self.assertEqual(report["version"], 1)
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in report["items"]],
                         ["a", "b", "c"])
        self.assertEqual([row["status"] for row in report["items"]],
                         ["verified", "invalid", "verified"])
        for row in report["items"]:
            self.assertEqual(list(row.keys()), ITEM_REPORT_KEYS)
        good = report["items"][0]
        self.assertIsNone(good["error"])
        self.assertEqual(good["result"]["proofDigest"],
                         hashlib.sha256(self.decision_a).hexdigest())
        self.assertEqual(list(good["result"].keys()), SINGLE_RESULT_KEYS)
        self.assertEqual(good["result"]["issuer"], JUDGE)
        bad = report["items"][1]
        self.assertIsNone(bad["result"])
        self.assertIsInstance(bad["error"], str)
        self.assertNotEqual(bad["error"], "")

    def test_unauthenticated_is_isolated(self):
        ring = {
            site: [entry(1, "77" * 32)]
            for site in (SITE_A, SITE_B, SITE_C, JUDGE)
        }
        report = self.batch_report([
            decision_item("a", self.decision_a),
            decision_item("b", self.decision_b),
        ], ring=ring)
        self.assertEqual([row["status"] for row in report["items"]],
                         ["unauthenticated", "unauthenticated"])
        self.assertTrue(all(row["error"] for row in report["items"]))
        self.assertTrue(all(row["result"] is None
                            for row in report["items"]))

    def test_structure_validated_upfront(self):
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.batch_report("x")
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.batch_report(["x"])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.batch_report([])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.batch_report([
                decision_item("a", self.decision_a),
                decision_item("a", self.decision_b),
            ])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.batch_report([
                {"id": "a", "decision": self.decision_a, "x": 1},
            ])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.batch_report([decision_item("", self.decision_a)])
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.batch_report([decision_item(1, self.decision_a)])
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.batch_report([decision_item("a", "x")])

    def test_shared_materials_validated_upfront(self):
        items = [decision_item("a", self.decision_a)]
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions(
                items, {"batch": "x"}, self.cauth(), self.ring, self.m)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions(
                items, self.policy, {"sites": {}}, self.ring, self.m)
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions(
                items, self.policy, self.cauth(), "ring", self.m)
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions(
                items, self.policy, self.cauth(), self.ring, True)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions(
                items, self.policy, self.cauth(), self.ring, -1)

    def test_batch_fault_surfaces_even_when_a_decision_is_bad(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.batch_report([
                decision_item("a", b"{}"), decision_item("a", b"{"),
            ])

    def test_one_result_matches_the_single_decision_result(self):
        report = self.batch_report([
            decision_item("ok", self.decision_a),
            decision_item("bad", b"{}"),
        ])
        single = verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decision(
            self.decision_a, self.policy, self.cauth(), self.ring, self.m)
        self.assertEqual(report["items"][0]["result"], single)

    def test_results_are_fresh_and_independent(self):
        items = [decision_item("a", self.decision_a)]
        first = self.batch_report(items)
        second = self.batch_report(items)
        self.assertEqual(first, second)
        self.assertIsNot(first, second)
        self.assertIsNot(first["items"][0]["result"],
                         second["items"][0]["result"])
        first["items"][0]["result"]["issuer"] = "tampered"
        self.assertEqual(
            self.batch_report(items)["items"][0]["result"]["issuer"], JUDGE)

    def test_inputs_are_not_modified(self):
        items = [decision_item("a", self.decision_a)]
        snapshot = copy.deepcopy((items, self.policy, self.cauth(), self.ring))
        self.batch_report(items)
        self.assertEqual(
            (items, self.policy, self.cauth(), self.ring), snapshot)


class AggregationValidationTest(
    ChainForkAggregateDecisionAggregateFixtures
):
    def test_items_container_and_value_faults(self):
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate("x")
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(["x"])
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate([decision_item(1, self.decision_a)])
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate([decision_item("a", 1)])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate([])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate([decision_item("", self.decision_a)])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate([
                decision_item("a", self.decision_a),
                decision_item("a", self.decision_b),
            ])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate([
                {"id": "a", "decision": self.decision_a, "x": 1},
            ])

    def test_policy_faults(self):
        items = self.cfa_decision_items()
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            aggregate_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions(
                items, {"batch": "x"}, self.cauth(), self.dsp, self.ring,
                self.m, JUDGE, 1)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(items, auth={"sites": {SITE_A: {1}}})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(items, dsp={"sites": {JUDGE: {1}}})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(items, dsp={"sites": {}, "threshold": 1})
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(
                items, dsp={"sites": {JUDGE: [1]}, "threshold": 1})
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(
                items, dsp={"sites": {JUDGE: {True}}, "threshold": 1})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(
                items, dsp={"sites": {JUDGE: {0}}, "threshold": 1})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(
                items, dsp={"sites": {JUDGE: set()}, "threshold": 1})
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(
                items, dsp={"sites": {JUDGE: {1}}, "threshold": True})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(
                items, dsp={"sites": {JUDGE: {1}}, "threshold": 0})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(
                items, dsp={"sites": {JUDGE: {1}}, "threshold": 2})

    def test_moment_issuer_version_rules(self):
        items = self.cfa_decision_items()
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(items, moment=True)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(items, moment=-1)
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(items, issuer=7)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(items, issuer="")
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(items, version=True)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(items, version=0)

    def test_signing_credentials_have_no_fallback(self):
        items = self.cfa_decision_items()
        with self.assertRaises(AuthenticationError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(items, issuer="nobody")
        with self.assertRaises(AuthenticationError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(items, issuer=JUDGE, version=2)
        revoked = dict(self.ring)
        revoked[JUDGE] = [entry(1, SECRET_COORD, revoked=True)]
        with self.assertRaises(AuthenticationError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(items, ring=revoked)
        future = dict(self.ring)
        future[JUDGE] = [entry(1, SECRET_COORD, not_before=self.m + 1)]
        with self.assertRaises(AuthenticationError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(items, ring=future)
        expired = dict(self.ring)
        expired[JUDGE] = [entry(1, SECRET_COORD, not_after=self.m - 1)]
        with self.assertRaises(AuthenticationError):
            self.make_cfa_aggregate(items, ring=expired)

    def test_inputs_are_not_modified(self):
        items = self.cfa_decision_items()
        snapshot = copy.deepcopy(
            (items, self.policy, self.cauth(), self.dsp, self.ring))
        self.make_cfa_aggregate(items)
        self.assertEqual(
            (items, self.policy, self.cauth(), self.dsp, self.ring),
            snapshot)


class PerItemRulingTest(ChainForkAggregateDecisionAggregateFixtures):
    def rows_by_id(self, items, **kwargs):
        payload = self.aggregate_payload(items, **kwargs)
        return {row["id"]: row for row in payload["items"]}

    def test_invalid_decision_rejected_alone_processing_continues(self):
        rows = self.rows_by_id([
            decision_item("good", self.decision_a),
            decision_item("bad", b"{}"),
            decision_item("good2", self.decision_b),
        ])
        bad = rows["bad"]
        self.assertEqual(bad["conclusion"], "invalid")
        self.assertEqual(bad["reason"], "invalid")
        self.assertIsNone(bad["issuer"])
        self.assertIsNone(bad["keyVersion"])
        self.assertIsNone(bad["declaration"])
        self.assertEqual(rows["good"]["conclusion"], "valid")
        self.assertEqual(rows["good2"]["conclusion"], "valid")

    def test_tampered_decision_binding_is_invalid_without_identity(self):
        payload = parse(self.decision_a)["payload"]
        payload["status"] = "insufficient"
        forged = rewrap(payload)
        rows = self.rows_by_id([decision_item("x", forged)])
        self.assertEqual(rows["x"]["reason"], "invalid")
        self.assertIsNone(rows["x"]["issuer"])

    def test_tampered_proof_digest_multiset_is_invalid_without_identity(self):
        # The proofs vector is order-independent but its digest multiset
        # must still cover exactly the per-row proof digests.
        payload = parse(self.decision_a)["payload"]
        payload["proofs"][0] = "ee" * 32
        forged = rewrap(payload)
        rows = self.rows_by_id([decision_item("x", forged)])
        self.assertEqual(rows["x"]["reason"], "invalid")
        self.assertIsNone(rows["x"]["issuer"])

    def test_foreign_policy_digest_is_invalid_without_identity(self):
        payload = parse(self.decision_a)["payload"]
        payload["prunePolicyDigest"] = "bb" * 32
        rows = self.rows_by_id([decision_item("x", rewrap(payload))])
        self.assertEqual(rows["x"]["reason"], "invalid")
        self.assertIsNone(rows["x"]["issuer"])

    def test_unauthenticated_states_keep_identity(self):
        dsp = decision_site_policy(sites=(JUDGE_B,), threshold=1)
        cases = [
            {JUDGE_B: [entry(2, "77" * 32)]},
            {JUDGE_B: [entry(1, SECRET_COORD, revoked=True)]},
            {JUDGE_B: [entry(1, SECRET_COORD, not_before=self.m + 1)]},
            {JUDGE_B: [entry(1, SECRET_COORD, not_after=self.m - 1)]},
        ]
        for overrides in cases:
            ring = dict(self.ring)
            ring.update(overrides)
            rows = self.rows_by_id(
                [decision_item("x", self.decision_b)], dsp=dsp, ring=ring)
            self.assertEqual(rows["x"]["conclusion"], "invalid")
            self.assertEqual(rows["x"]["reason"], "unauthenticated")
            self.assertEqual(rows["x"]["issuer"], JUDGE_B)
            self.assertEqual(rows["x"]["keyVersion"], 1)
            self.assertIsNone(rows["x"]["declaration"])

        forged = rewrap(parse(self.decision_b)["payload"], secret="77" * 32)
        rows = self.rows_by_id([decision_item("x", forged)], dsp=dsp)
        self.assertEqual(rows["x"]["reason"], "unauthenticated")
        self.assertEqual(rows["x"]["issuer"], JUDGE_B)

    def test_unauthorized_site_and_version_keep_identity(self):

        # Reversing the proof summaries keeps each decision individually

        # includes the proof summary sequence: any same-site declaration
        # difference is a contradiction, never a duplicate.
        decision_payload = parse(self.decision_a)["payload"]
        decision_payload["proofs"] = list(reversed(decision_payload["proofs"]))

            decision_item("first", self.decision_a),
            decision_item("second", reordered),
        ], dsp=dsp)
        self.assertEqual(payload["status"], "conflicted")
        self.assertIsNone(payload["declaration"])
        self.assertEqual(
            [row["conclusion"] for row in payload["items"]],
            ["contradiction", "contradiction"])

class CrossEntryCompatibilityTest(
    ChainForkAggregateDecisionAggregateFixtures
):
    """A legal decision is accepted consistently by every decision entry.

    The single decision verifier, the decision batch verifier and the
    cross-site aggregator (and its own verifier) must agree on what a
    legal chain fork aggregate decision is: the proof summary vector is
    bound as an order-independent multiset over the site/id-sorted rows,
    so reversing the summaries and re-signing stays legal, while
    replacing a summary with a foreign digest is rejected by all three.
    """

    def _outcomes(self, raw):
        try:
            verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decision(
                raw, self.policy, self.cauth(), self.ring, self.m)
            single = "ok"
        except InvalidChainDecisionError:
            single = "invalid"
        except AuthenticationError:
            single = "unauth"
        batch = verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions(
            [decision_item("i", raw)], self.policy, self.cauth(),
            self.ring, self.m,
        )["items"][0]["status"]
        aggregate = aggregate_chain_fork_aggregate_decisions(
            [decision_item("i", raw)], self.policy, self.cauth(), self.dsp,
            self.ring, self.m, JUDGE, 1,
        )
        row = parse(aggregate)["payload"]["items"][0]
        aggregate_verifies = True
        try:
            verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decision_aggregate(
                aggregate, self.policy, self.cauth(), self.dsp, self.ring,
                self.m)
        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - any divergence fails below
            aggregate_verifies = False
        return single, batch, (row["conclusion"], row["reason"]), (
            aggregate_verifies)

    def test_legal_decisions_accepted_everywhere(self):
        for raw in (self.decision_a, self.decision_b):
            single, batch, row, verifies = self._outcomes(raw)
            self.assertEqual(single, "ok")
            self.assertEqual(batch, "verified")
            self.assertEqual(row, ("valid", None))
            self.assertTrue(verifies)

    def test_reversed_proof_summaries_accepted_everywhere(self):
        payload = parse(self.decision_a)["payload"]
        payload["proofs"] = list(reversed(payload["proofs"]))
        reordered = rewrap(payload)
        single, batch, row, verifies = self._outcomes(reordered)
        self.assertEqual(single, "ok")
        self.assertEqual(batch, "verified")
        self.assertEqual(row, ("valid", None))
        self.assertTrue(verifies)

    def test_foreign_proof_summary_rejected_everywhere(self):
        payload = parse(self.decision_a)["payload"]
        payload["proofs"][0] = "ee" * 32
        forged = rewrap(payload)
        single, batch, row, verifies = self._outcomes(forged)
        self.assertEqual(single, "invalid")
        self.assertEqual(batch, "invalid")
        self.assertEqual(row, ("invalid", "invalid"))
        self.assertTrue(verifies)

    def test_bound_declaration_proof_sequence_is_fixed(self):
        # Reordering the common declaration's proof sequence inside an
        # otherwise valid aggregate breaks its equality with the row
        # declarations and is rejected even after re-signing.
        raw = self.make_cfa_aggregate(self.cfa_decision_items())
        payload = parse(raw)["payload"]
        declaration = payload["declaration"]
        declaration["proofs"] = list(reversed(declaration["proofs"]))
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainForkDecisionAggregateError):
            self.verify_aggregate(rewrap(payload))

33263	def verify_chain_fork_aggregate_decision_aggregate(
33264	    aggregate, prune_policy, authorization_policy, decision_site_policy,
33265	    keyring, moment,
33266	):
33267	    """Verify a signed chain fork aggregate decision aggregate offline.
33268	
33269	    Only the aggregate bytes, the expected shared ``prune_policy``, the
33270	    expected site ``authorization_policy``, the expected
33271	    ``decision_site_policy``, the current ``keyring`` and the
33272	    verification ``moment`` are consulted -- no file is read or written
33273	    and no argument is modified.  Verification validates the canonical
33274	    encoding and every key set, recomputes all three policy digests, and
33275	    re-tallies the bound per-decision rows purely from the signed
33276	    payload: the original-order input digest bindings, the issuer/id
33277	    row ordering, same-site duplicate and contradiction markings,
33278	    cross-site complete declaration agreement (the common fork edge
33279	    set, the per-item conclusions, the original-order proof digest
33280	    vector and the overall status together), the threshold outcome and
33281	    the claimed common declaration, together with a full re-tally of
33282	    every counted declaration against the authorization policy
33283	    threshold.  It then checks the HMAC-SHA256 against the key the
33284	    *current* keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and version,
33285	    usable at the verification moment, so a later revocation or expiry
33286	    rejects the aggregate with no fallback.
33287	
33288	    On success a fresh dict equal to the authenticated payload plus
33289	    ``aggregateDigest`` (the SHA-256 of the aggregate bytes) is
33290	    returned with the fixed keys ``aggregateDigest``, ``inputs``,
33291	    ``issuer``, ``items``, ``keyVersion``, ``prunePolicyDigest``,
33292	    ``authorizationPolicyDigest``, ``decisionSitePolicyDigest``,
33293	    ``declaration``, ``status`` and ``version`` (the integer 1) --
33294	    repeated calls return equal but mutually independent objects
33295	    sharing no mutable structure.  A non-bytes aggregate or a field of
33296	    the wrong type raises :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never
33297	    poses as an int); a null value, a duplicate id, a wrong key set or
33298	    an illegal policy, threshold or other value raises
33299	    :class:`ValueError`; an illegal encoding, key set, digest,
33300	    ordering, tally or declaration binding raises
33301	    :class:`InvalidChainForkDecisionAggregateError` (a
33302	    :class:`ValueError` subclass); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or
33303	    expired credentials or a signature mismatch raise
33304	    :class:`AuthenticationError`.

33307	        raise TypeError("aggregate packet must be bytes")

33309	    validated_authorization_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(

33311	    )
